**[Ca2+ is an intracellular danger signal promoting STING activation.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42976867/)** *(from Cell biology / calcium signaling and virology (innate antiviral host defense))*  
*Zhou Nanhai; Gao Pengfei; Zhao Han; Liu Qiyu; Wang Xurui* — Molecular cell 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NF-kB-IKK, treatment-target, other`  
> The paper identifies a Ca2+-CaM-CaMKK-CaMK1D cascade as a required second signal for STING phosphorylation and TBK1 trans-autophosphorylation, a novel control point on the cGAS-STING-TBK1-IRF3 axis (Loop A) that drives IFN-I in the SAMHD1 A565T interferonopathy. It also suggests druggable nodes (CaMK1D, SOCE/ORAI, TRPV2) for tuning interferonopathy amplitude, and it connects to VDAC1 and mitochondrial Ca2+ dysregulation. It contains no SAMHD1, mtDNA, NLRP3 or mitochondrial dNTP data, so the link is indirect.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.molcel.2026.10.008

**[Mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1 axis mediates hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment by driving hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PPR1355196)** *(from High-altitude/hypoxia medicine and neuroscience (neuronal ferroptosis and cognitive impairment))*  
*Chen Qian; Zheng Handan; Hao Xiaokang; Feng Yujie; Zhu Yiyi* —  2026  
Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, POLG-mtDNA, treatment-target, VDAC1, clinical-phenotype, other`  
> Shows that mtDNA release from damaged mitochondria activates cGAS-STING, which drives neuronal ferroptosis (via a STING-CISD1/mitoNEET interaction at mito-ER contacts) and cognitive impairment, and that STING inhibition with C-176 rescues the phenotype. This mirrors the family's mtDNA escape to cGAS-STING axis (Blue stream) and offers neuro-cognitive and STING-targeting treatment implications. It has no SAMHD1, dNTP, NLRP3 or ISG15 data, and the hypoxia context and ferroptosis endpoint are only indirectly connected to the A565T interferon-mitochondrial syndrome.  
DOI: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-11392101/v1
